items.note: Abstract: long-term analysis finds several meteorological stations of the Betwa basin with decreasing annual and seasonal precipitation and fewer rainy days; onset of effective monsoon shows no trend except at Shivpuri and Tikamgarh.
Abstract: maximum and minimum temperature trends in the Betwa basin (winter increases); increased winter temperature may adversely affect Rabi crops (wheat and mustard).

Betwa basin is 'historically important' but underdeveloped for lack of irrigation facilities; agriculture is the mainstay and the area, especially upper and middle regions, is prone to famines and droughts.
Betwa basin extent: 77°10'E–80°20'E, 22°54'–26°05'N, about 43,500 km2; river length 590 km, of which 232 km in Madhya Pradesh and 358 km in Uttar Pradesh.

Basin climate: moderate, mostly dry except southwest monsoon; rainfall 700-1,200 mm (average 1,138 mm), evaporation about 1,830 mm, runoff about 13,430 MCM (80% in monsoon); temperature 42.3 to 8.1 °C; humidity 18% to 90%.

items.note: Rainfall trends 1901-2001: in the monsoon season Berasia and Sehore show decreasing trends while Vidisha shows an increasing trend (slope 2.79); Basoda, Lalitpur, Sehore and Vidisha show persistence.
Based on the basin-average MK statistic, no significant trend was observed in summer, winter, monsoon or yearly rainfall in the basin.
Rainy-day trends 1973-2003: winter rainy days decreasing at Bhopal, Hamirpur, Shivpuri and Tikamgarh; yearly rainy days decreasing at Begumganj, Hamirpur, Tikamgarh, Shivpuri and Korwai.

items.note: No significant basin trend in rainy days; defines onset of effective monsoon (OEM) as an agro-climatic variable for planning agricultural operations (land preparation, sowing) for Kharif crops, with its rainfall criteria.
Onset of effective monsoon: Shivpuri and Tikamgarh show increasing trend (delayed onset); no significant trend in OEM for the basin overall.
